recipes.name: Wonton Wrappers
ingredients_raw: 0.33333334326744 cup water, or more as needed

steps.text: Beat egg in a medium bowl. Mix in 1/3 cup water.
Combine flour and salt in a large bowl. Create a well in the center of the flour mixture and slowly pour in egg and water.
Mix well. If the mixture is too dry, increase the amount of water 1 teaspoon at a time until a pliable dough has formed.
Knead dough on a lightly floured surface until elastic.
Cut dough into two separate balls. Cover dough balls with a damp cloth for a minimum of 10 minutes.
Cut each ball into four equal pieces.
Roll the pieces into 10 ½ x 10 ½-inch squares. Then cut each square into nine 3 ½ x 3 ½-inch squares for a total of 72 wonton wrappers. Use in any wonton recipe.

raw_recipe.headline: Wonton Wrappers
raw_recipe.description: Make wonton wrappers from scratch with this homemade step-by-step recipe to create tasty little dumplings stuffed with your favorite fillings.

review.reviewBody: I used for potstickers... YUM!!! If you are one of the unlucky rolling these out by hand, I found that rolling out each of your 4 pieces into a square smaller than recommended, cutting into 9 equal smaller squares, and then rolling each square individually to size worked best for me, and there was no problem getting them thin enough using this method. Do yourself a favor and fill each one (or have a helper do it) as you roll it out - I had a horrible time with them sticking together having put the finished wrappers in a big stack and ended up wasting most of a batch. But the few potstickers I managed to make were so good that I saved my filling for the next day and tried again. A lot of work but well worth it!

Turned out great. I read the reviews from others who tried to make this before. I used my kitchen aid mixer which helped a ton. I had to add an extra 1/4 cup of water as the dough was very crumbly. I added 1 teaspoon of water at a time until it finally formed a dough ball. So total was 1/4 cup of water. I let the dough rest for 30 mins. Then used my kitchen aid pasta roller attachment. Saved me so much time.
Made these but I used corn starch to flour the board when rolling them out which made them crisper. Love doing things like this instead buying premade

Since I didn’t have any wonton wrappers on hand this recipe definitely came in handy. I used ingredients that I had on hand. I would suggest reading reviews to make this recipe easier. More water is needed, I added a teaspoon at a time. Letting the dough rest an hour made the dough easier to roll out. Also, using cornstarch to dust the waxed paper before rolling out.

Quick tip. Use a food processor and pulse it to bring the dough together. Knead it for a few minutes like you would pizza dough. I have a Marcato Atlas Wellness 150 Pasta Maker and I highly recommend it rather than rolling them out by hand. I make the wontons into 5" by 6" rectangles and make my own hot pockets. Put in pepperoni, mozzarella, and marinara sauce. Fry them up and then freeze them for quick lunches. MUCH better and cheaper than buying them at the store.

I used my Kitchen Aid blending machine to merge and knead the ingredients obtaining pliable dough that possibly could serve as base for shredding into noodles as well. The wrappers rolled out of this dough yielded smooth and firm (or as the chinese would say: tan ya or jin dao) wontons proving a delight for both the palate and the eye. The result was also due to that as flour only using Manitoba type ditto designed for pizza baking. Sure, it demanded a lot of ardous effort, but the result was worth all and every bit of that.

Stoked I took the time to read reviews. Definitely cover with a warm towl and let rise for 30-45 minutes. I happen to be an extra unfortunate individual with nooo rolling pin. Took my bamboo cutting board and dusted it with flower. Flattened the dough out best I could by hand , pizza crust style. Then, with a dough scraper, cut the circle into six equal slices. Flattened out each piece and broke again into four pieces. Rolled all of the pieces into balls, let rest on parchment paper in between the board. I floured my board again and flattened each circle first with my palm, and then with the bottom of a measuring cup, also sprinkled in flour. I used the scraper to cut each circle into a square, then gave them on final mash. Made a few more with the circle scraps. Drained and pressed a can of spinach (usually use frozen, but had none on hand), sauteed 3/4 of an onion with a can of mushrooms in 2tbs butter, then tossed them in my mixer with 8oz room temp cream cheese. Filled the wraps and fried in sunflower oil. Made a dipping sauce with a little soy sauce, orange juice, and a tiny bit of oil/flour roux. Superb!

This was an easy recipe. I followed it with a couple of exceptions. 1) I neaded for 10+ minutes to increase elasticity 2) let dough rest for an hour to relax gluten 3) used plenty of cornstarch when rolling. These slight adjustments made it a lot easier to form the noodles. Oh yes, I made these entirely by hand.... No food processor, mixer or pasta press.

Just made them and added my home made mixture of ground pork mixed with ginger, garlic, a little sesame oil and soy sauce, then rolled into little balls and fried them. Once cooled, I scrunched the rolled out wrappers around each fried pork ball. Made dashi broth, added bok choy, fresh ginger slices, sliced fresh shiitake mushrooms and brought the soup to a boil. Once the wontons floated, I cooked for a few minutes and enjoyed with my husband. It was delicious. Next time I just need to roll out the wrappers a wee bit thinner. Recipe definitely a keeper for future dishes. thank you so much.

This takes a while to do. Rolling it out is a pain if you don't have a pasta machine. But I was set on making crab rangoons for a potluck and of course, none of the food markets that were open at 9 pm had wonton wrappers. 

So overall, great recipe. Everyone was incredibly impressed that I made everything by hand but it was a simple, foolproof recipe. I ran out of time so instead of resting with a damp cloth, I wrapped it in plastic wrap and let sit overnight in the fridge. Let it rest on the counter for about 10 minutes then rolled out with plenty of cornstarch. Don't use flour when rolling out. It will make it tacky. Use cornstarch!

This recipe worked out perfectly! I did need to add a bit more water, but that was all. The key to this dough is to allow it sit, covered at room temp to rest for easier rolling. The dough was beautiful to work with. I actually made the dough the day before, wrapped it and put it in the fridge. The next morning I took it out to come to room temp and 'rest'. I used a pasta machine to roll the dough to the thickness I wanted. Very easy and VERY delicious, waaaay better than store bought (and cheaper too)...A definite keeper~YUM! Thanks for sharing. :)
Dough was a little hard to work with. Next time I'd add extra water by the teaspoon instead of tablespoon. I did make myself a very addicting batch of deep-fried elote chips with this recipe!
I just made my first batch, I will come back and share how they worked out for me.
Made these this afternoon and oh my... I'm never going back to store bought dough... my picky eater LOVED them and asked me to make more. I would say these are hit in my house!
My first time making wantons and I am very impressed. Great recipe!

Made this tonight! Used a pasta machine down to #7 and they were fabulous! Next time we'll go to #8 or 9 to see if they can be more delicate. Easy, quick, and tasted amazing. We will never buy won tons again. :)

I did add about an extra 1/4 cup water to get a good dough. I stirred it with a fork and dumped out on cornstarch then gave it a few kneads and covered and let rest for about an hour. It didn’t look like it raised or anything. I did cut into smaller pieces. Rolled them out with rolling pin and fried them up to go with crab Rangoon dip.
I love this recipe! It was really fun to make and even more fun to eat! I will definitely make this again! It made about 24 dumplings that were palm sized.

Really good. I used to make cream cheese wontons when I forgot to buy wrappers from the store. They don't turn out quite as crispy as store bought wontons when you fry, but my family said they actually preferred these. Will use again.
